newsitem.title: USA: Three citizens' militiamen convicted in Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Three citizens' militiamen convicted in Georgia.

text.p: A federal jury on Wednesday convicted three members of a Georgia militia group on charges they conspired to use pipe bombs in a war against the U.S. government.
After a three-week trial, jurors emerged from five days of deliberations to return guilty verdicts against militia leader Robert Starr, Jimmy McCranie and Troy Spain.
Each man could face more than 20 years in prison. Sentencing was set for January.
The three defendants -- an electrician, a plumber and a contractor -- belonged to a group calling itself the 112th Regiment, Militia-at-Large for the Republic of Georgia.

The FBI accused them of conspiring to stockpile weapons for a retaliatory strike against any move against them by federal agents. The men allegedly drew up a list of potential targets including bridges, vehicles, power lines and federal law enforcement officials.

The jury found them guilty on charges of possessing pipe bombs and conspiring to use them against the government. But they were found not guilty on three other counts, including a charge involving alleged threats against an agent with the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms.

"Thankfully, the laws of this state and the nation give us the right to go in on a conspiracy count. We can stop something like this from happening before it does," said assistant U.S. Attorney Sharon Ratley.
"That's why we try conspiracy cases and why we're able to stop tragedies such as what could have happened."
Starr, 35, and McCranie, 30, were arrested last April after informants led federal agents to buried explosives on Starr's property. Spain, 28, turned himself in a month later.

Early news reports said the men were planning an attack on the 1996 Summer Games in Atlanta. Although federal officials quickly denied that claim, prosecution witnesses testified that the three did talk about planting explosives-laden lunch boxes at the Olympics.
On July 27, a pipe bomb hidden in an army-style knapsack exploded during a free concert at Centennial Olympic Park in Atlanta, leaving two dead and more than 100 injured. The case remains unsolved.
